title: Rav Acha, brother of Mar Achai
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Mentioned in [Shabbat 111b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.111b.7) according to Hyman’s report of all the old printings and the reading known to Yuchasin. The text he calls “our reading” is: “Rav Achadvoi, brother of Mar Acha—or from Acha—asked.”

notes.text: דמן אחא means “from Acha,” not “of Mar Acha.” The exact relation of this alternative qualifier to the preceding brother designation remains unresolved.

[Rabbeinu Chananel](https://www.sefaria.org/Rabbeinu_Chananel_on_Shabbat.111b.5) takes Acha as a place. [Maharshal](https://www.sefaria.org/Chokhmat_Shlomo_on_Shabbat.112a.1) gives the brother wording, then quotes “from Acha” as a variant. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=317&lang=en) discusses the same two forms and the separate occurrence in [Kiddushin 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.22b.18).

In the consulted Vilna edition, Rabbeinu Chananel on Shabbat 111b takes the phrase as a place name. Maharshal’s Chokhmat Shlomo, catalogued at Shabbat 112a:1, gives the brother reading and records “from Acha” as an alternative, citing Tosafot Shantz in Rabbeinu Chananel’s name. Kiddushin 22b has a separate occurrence of Rav Achai [bar Adda] from Acha. The exact old printings and the passage in Yuchasin still need collation.
